components.name: body
components.description: Pinned checksum-era generation uses 37 alphanumeric characters and six base62 checksum characters; pre-checksum generation constraints remain unresolved.

claims.statement: prefix: polar_pat_, polar_at_u_, polar_at_o_, polar_rt_u_, polar_rt_o_, polar_cs_ or polar_crt_
boundary: a token glued to an identifier on either side ([A-Za-z0-9_-]) is not claimed (Handoff boundary decision, not a provider statement.)
At the pinned server revision, generate_token appends 37 ASCII letters or digits followed by six zero-padded base62 CRC32 characters to the prefix.

sources.supports: The generator concatenates 37 alphanumeric characters and six checksum characters.

claims.statement: The pre-checksum body length and alphabet are unresolved as provider-backed constraints; revision 1 relied on the Python default of an argument-free token_urlsafe call rather than an explicit Polar guarantee.

The confidentiality classification of polar_ci_ OAuth client identifiers is unresolved: the constants declare a client-id prefix without classifying confidentiality, while the OAuth setup documentation directs users to keep both client ID and client secret secret.

sources.supports: Defines CLIENT_ID_PREFIX but does not classify its confidentiality.
Directs users to keep client ID and client secret secret.
sources.locator: Create your client, paragraphs after the client settings

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Proposed correction of revision 1 provider-source, field-body-length, field-alphabet and field-public-and-short-lived-siblings overclaims. Current checksum-era constraints are separated from unresolved historical constraints; no union-era descriptivePattern is asserted. Unrelated imported meta-claims, transport and peer assertions are not reasserted. Original revision, currentContract and all fixture expectations remain unchanged.

openQuestions.question: Does Polar classify polar_ci_ client IDs as confidential or public, and how should the setup-page confidentiality warning be reconciled with public-client usage?
What scanner-neutral expectation applies when a complete token is adjacent to extra identifier characters? A provider statement or explicit reviewed project policy is needed.

What provider guarantee establishes length and alphabet for credentials emitted before checksum generation? A dependency-default derivation must identify its version and remain separate from a Polar guarantee.
Were access tokens without a subtype suffix ever issued and can any remain valid?
Does sharing a checkout URL establish that its polar_cl_ component is safe to publish independently or in arbitrary contexts?
